req.title: Logout clears session
req.statement: The system shall clear the session and redirect to / on GET /auth/logout.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /auth/logout must clear the session and redirect to / with a 302 status. I design: (1) a positive test confirming a logged-in user is redirected to / with status 302 and session cleared (STC — logged-in → logged-out state transition); (2) a negative test confirming an already-logged-out (anonymous) user hitting /auth/logout still gets 302 to / and session remains clear (NEG — no session to clear); (3) a boundary test confirming the redirect Location header is exactly '/' and not any other path, and that 'user_id' is absent from the session after logout (BVA — exact constant check on redirect target and session key). Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill status-code, redirect-target, and session-key mutations.

tests.name: test_logout_clears_session_and_redirects_logged_in_user
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with fixture data (user id=1, username='test', password='test')
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
expected: Session no longer contains 'user_id' after logout
trace: STC: state transition from authenticated to anonymous
Catches mutations: status 302->301/303, location '/'->'auth/login', session.clear() removal
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'test'
login_resp = client.post(
    '/auth/login',
    data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'}
)
assert login_resp.status_code == 302, f"Login failed: {login_resp.status_code}"

# Confirm session has user_id before logout
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' in sess
    assert sess['user_id'] == 1

# Perform logout
logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_resp.status_code == 302
assert logout_resp.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Confirm session is cleared
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_logout_redirect_location_is_exactly_root_not_subpath
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with fixture data
actions: Inspect Location header character by character
expected: Location header equals exactly '/' (length 1, not '/auth/login', not '/index', not '')
Status code is exactly 302 (not 301, not 303, not 200)
After logout, a GET to a login-required page redirects to /auth/login (confirming session is truly cleared)
trace: R-FLASKR-011: redirect target must be exactly '/'

STC: post-logout access to protected resource confirms session cleared end-to-end
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in
login_resp = client.post(
    '/auth/login',
    data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'}
)
assert login_resp.status_code == 302

# Logout and check exact redirect
logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_resp.status_code == 302
location = logout_resp.headers['Location']
assert location == '/', f"Expected '/' got {location!r}"
assert location != '/auth/login'
assert location != '/auth/logout'
assert location != ''
assert len(location) == 1

# Confirm session truly cleared: accessing /create redirects to login
create_resp = client.get('/create')
assert create_resp.status_code == 302
assert create_resp.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_logout_session_user_id_absent_after_multiple_logouts
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with fixture data
User 'test' logs in, logs out, then logs in again
expected: After each logout session has no 'user_id'
trace: R-FLASKR-011: session cleared on every logout invocation
BVA: repeated login/logout cycle — catches mutations where session.clear() is skipped on second call
STC: logged-out -> logged-in -> logged-out state cycle
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

for cycle in range(2):
    r_login = client.post(
        '/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'}
    )
    assert r_login.status_code == 302, f"cycle {cycle} login failed"
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert sess.get('user_id') == 1, f"cycle {cycle} user_id missing after login"

    r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r_logout.status_code == 302, f"cycle {cycle} logout status wrong"
    assert r_logout.headers['Location'] == '/', f"cycle {cycle} wrong redirect"
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' not in sess, f"cycle {cycle} user_id still in session"

os.unlink(path)

expected: Status code is 302 (not 200, not 301, not 303, not 404, not 500)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'other' (id=2)
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
assert r.status_code == 302
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert sess.get('user_id') == 2

# Logout
logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_resp.status_code == 302
assert logout_resp.status_code != 200
assert logout_resp.status_code != 301
assert logout_resp.status_code != 303
assert logout_resp.status_code != 404
assert logout_resp.status_code != 500
assert logout_resp.headers['Location'] == '/'

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

os.unlink(path)
